die_note: 2 graphics compute dies (GCDs) in one OAM package, 220 CUs
scale_up: Infinity Fabric, 8 links x 100 GB/s each
summary: Previous-generation CDNA 2 accelerator with strong FP64, used in exascale supercomputers such as Frontier.
notes: FP16/BF16 383 TFLOPS and INT8 383 TOPS as listed by AMD (dense; no sparsity). FP32 matrix 95.7. TDP listed as 500 W | 560 W peak; 560 used. Transistor count not on page. No FP8.
variants_note: MI250: 128 GB, lower clocks (not on fetched page).

die_note: Single die, 24 TPC, 2 MME, 48 MB SRAM
scale_up: 24x100 GbE RoCE v2 on-chip, 600 GB/s bidirectional
summary: Second-generation Habana training accelerator with 96 GB HBM2e and integrated Ethernet for scale-out.
notes: BF16/FP8 are matrix-engine (MME) peaks from Intel white paper; BF16 vector 11 TFLOPS. Networking is Ethernet, not a proprietary scale-up fabric. Bandwidth 2.45-2.46 TB/s across Intel docs.

die_note: 2 compute dies joined by interposer bridge, 64 TPC, 8 MME, 96 MB SRAM, 8 HBM2e stacks
scale_up: 24x200 GbE RoCE v2 on-chip, 1,200 GB/s bidirectional
summary: Intel's third-generation Gaudi with 128 GB HBM2e and 24 integrated 200 GbE ports for Ethernet-based clusters.
notes: Intel documents conflict: Hot Chips 2024 and a later white paper copy give 1835 BF16/FP8 matrix TFLOPS; another white paper revision and the 30-3-30 sheet give 1678. 1835 used. Bandwidth 3.67 TB/s (3.7 rounded). Same peak for BF16 and FP8. No sparsity.
variants_note: Liquid-cooled variant up to 1200 W (Hot Chips 2024); HLB-325 PCIe card also exists (not covered).

die_note: 1 TensorCore per chip, 2D torus ICI, 256-chip pod
scale_up: ICI 2D torus, 400 GB/s bidirectional per chip
summary: Cost-efficient Google Cloud TPU for smaller-scale training and inference.
notes: Google lists HBM bandwidth as 800 GiB/s (~0.86 TB/s). Dense figures; Google quotes INT8 393 TOPS. Power, process and FP8 not published.

die_note: 2 TensorCores + 4 SparseCores per chip, 3D torus, 8,960-chip pod
scale_up: ICI 3D torus, 1,200 GB/s bidirectional per chip
summary: Google's large-scale training TPU generation with 95 GiB HBM per chip.
notes: Memory listed by Google as 95 GiB. Docs table lists FP8 equal to BF16 (459), so no FP8 speedup is claimed there; treat fp8 value cautiously. Power and process not published.

die_note: 1 TensorCore per chip, 2 MXU, 2D torus, 256-chip pod
scale_up: ICI 2D torus, 800 GB/s bidirectional per chip
summary: Trillium, Google's cost-efficient 2024 TPU with 32 GB HBM and 918 BF16 TFLOPS.
notes: Google lists INT8 1836 TOPS; the TPU7x comparison table lists FP8 918 for v6e but v6e page does not, so fp8 left null. Power and process not published.

die_note: Dual-chiplet: 2 TensorCores, 4 SparseCores, 2x96 GB HBM; 3D torus up to 9,216 chips
scale_up: ICI 3D torus, 1,200 GB/s bidirectional per chip
summary: Google's seventh-generation TPU with 192 GB HBM and FP8 support, built for large training and inference pods.
notes: Google docs name it TPU7x (Ironwood). HBM listed as 192 GiB, 7,380 GB/s. Docs table shows 2307 BF16 and 4614 FP8 peak. Power and process not published.

die_note: 2 NeuronCore-v2
scale_up: NeuronLink-v2 (per-chip bandwidth not found in fetched docs)
summary: AWS's first-generation training chip, available in Trn1 instances with 32 GiB HBM.
notes: Neuron docs: 190 TFLOPS FP16/BF16/cFP8/TF32; fp8 is configurable FP8 (cFP8). 32 GiB, 820 GiB/s as published (0.82 used). Release year from general knowledge, not verified in fetched pages.

die_note: 8 NeuronCore-v3, 16 CC-cores
summary: AWS's second-generation training chip with 96 GiB HBM, used in Trn2 instances and UltraServers.
notes: Dense: 1,299 FP8 and 667 BF16/FP16/TF32 TFLOPS. AWS also quotes 2,563 sparse TFLOPS (not used). Memory listed in GiB. NeuronLink bandwidth direction not specified.

die_note: 2 NeuronCore-v2
scale_up: NeuronLink-v2 (AWS figures conflict: 384 GB/s per chip in blog, 192 GB/s on Inf2 page)
summary: AWS inference-focused chip with 32 GiB HBM, used in Inf2 instances.
notes: Same NeuronCore-v2 compute as Trainium1: 190 FP16/BF16/cFP8/TF32 TFLOPS. Inference part; included under Training family per assignment.

die_note: Single die, 20 AI cores (Da Vinci)
summary: Huawei's SMIC-made 2023 training NPU, a main China-market alternative to NVIDIA A100-class parts.
notes: Huawei has not published an official datasheet. 294.9 TFLOPS FP16 cube peak from an arXiv academic paper; aggregator flopper.io (citing CSET) claims 400 TFLOPS FP16 and 1.6 TB/s, which conflicts. Bandwidth 1.6 TB/s from aggregator only. Variants (910B1-B4) differ.
variants_note: Earlier 910B1 samples had 32 GB; flopper.io lists 400 W TDP (unverified).

die_note: Dual-die package, 128 GB HBM
scale_up: Unified Bus (UB), ~2,800 Gb/s unidirectional per chip (SemiAnalysis via secondary source)
summary: Huawei's dual-die 2025 AI accelerator used in CloudMatrix pods, roughly 800 FP16 TFLOPS with 128 GB HBM.
notes: 800 TFLOPS FP16, 128 GB, 3.2 TB/s from Tom's Hardware (Huawei roadmap). An arXiv paper gives 378.9 per die (~758 per package) which differs. scale_up_gbs = 2,800 Gb/s unidirectional = 350 GB/s x2 bidirectional, derived. Memory type HBM2e per aggregator, unverified. TDP not published.
